# update_llm_file_tool

> Update existing LlmFile records with new content, title, or directory location.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | `data` |
| Callable | MCP clients; in-app @ai conversations (default); grantable to agents |
| Filter | `https://www.dsiloed.com/api/v1/mcp?tools=update_llm_file_tool` |

## Description

This is the description the server sends to the model, verbatim.

Update existing LlmFile records with new content, title, or directory location.
This tool allows AI agents to modify existing documents (reports, summaries, documentation) with updated information.

Content, title and directory_path can each be updated alone or together.

RULES:
- `content` replaces the ENTIRE file. For a small change to a large file use
  `replacements` (find/replace) instead of resending the whole thing.
- MIME type cannot be changed — create a new file if the type must change. (One healing
  exception: a TEXT file stored as application/octet-stream is re-declared to its real
  text type when its content is updated.)
- Every content rewrite first snapshots the previous body as an LlmDocVersion, so the
  old content stays recoverable.
- Conversation attachments and relationships survive the update.
- Text content only; for binary files use the file upload API.
- Describe what you changed when you report back.

CROSS-TENANT: a file shared with you from another tenant resolves automatically when the
id is not in your tenant — but only with EDITOR access or higher, and only for title/content
updates. Viewer-level shares are read-only (use read_llm_file_tool). directory_path cannot
be changed on cross-tenant files (reorganizing is the owning tenant's concern).

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `llm_file_id` | integer | yes | ID of the LlmFile to update (required) |
| `title` | string | no | New title for the file (optional). If provided, will replace the existing title. |
| `content` | string | no | New document content (optional). Completely REPLACES existing content. For a small change to a large file, prefer `replacements` so you need not resend the whole file. |
| `replacements` | array of object | no | Targeted find/replace edits applied to the EXISTING file server-side — use instead of `content` to edit part of a large text file (HTML, markdown, ...) without resending it. Each item replaces ALL literal (non-regex) occurrences of `find` with `replace`. Errors if a `find` is not present (no silent no-op). Ignored when `content` is also given. |
| `directory_path` | string | no | New virtual directory path for file organization (optional). If provided, moves the file to the new directory (e.g., "/projects/docs", "/reports/2024") |

## Example

Targeted edit of a large document without resending it:

```json
{"name": "update_llm_file_tool", "arguments": {"llm_file_id": 3672, "replacements": [{"find": "Capital: $20k", "replace": "Capital: $30k"}]}}
```

Full replacement (small files):

```json
{"name": "update_llm_file_tool", "arguments": {"llm_file_id": 3672, "content": "# Plan v2\n\n..."}}
```

## Gotchas

- **`content` replaces everything.** Prefer `replacements` for a change to part of a file.
- **Moving a file** is `directory_path` here, or `move_llm_file_tool` for renames and bulk moves.
